deviations.description: Omit the two interactive View() calls for headless execution; retain all original files unchanged.
Copy source lines 272–758 (Group 1 analysis), substituting BM→HWG, Group1→Group2 and group1→group2, to supply the explicitly omitted Group 2 block.

Treat the five blank Group 2 binary task responses as unsuccessful (0): Task5_GM 1, Task4_HWG 1, Task5_HWG 3. This is consistent with the paper scoring description and the shipped STAT NA→0 step, but is not executable shipped Group 2 code. Preserve minimal-repair outputs without this assumption for comparison.

Evaluate the original SUS input/scoring definitions (source lines 1045–1084) before the cross-group analysis that consumes those objects at lines 774 onward. Original later definitions remain unchanged.

Compute the omitted four HWG Kendall correlations using the paper-described test and the same R cor.test(method="kendall",exact=FALSE) pattern. Match rows by participant ID; audit confirms existing file order is aligned.

Capture the original Google Maps SUS–task correlation before the final source lines overwrite SUS_GMCorrelation with a STAT correlation; export full-precision test fields separately from rounded display matrices.

tolerance_policy.ordinary_numbers: Half a unit in the last reported decimal (means/SD/statistics/tau 2 decimals; alpha/p 3; integer counts exact).
tolerance_policy.confidence_intervals: Paper display precision (Table 4/5 one decimal; Table 8 GM-HWG one decimal and other limits two decimals), plus 0.001 for the numerical interval solver.
tolerance_policy.p_inequalities: A reported p < .001 is checked literally.
tolerance_policy.claim_group_rule: A claim group is reproduced only when every compared field matches. Matching p-values or signs alone does not erase a mismatched statistic or interval.
tolerance_policy.figures: Figures recreated using the original plotting calls (Group 2 reconstructed). Data aggregates and selected rendered plots inspected; no pixel-perfect comparison claimed.

limitations: The required public rule pack and certificate schema returned HTTP 404. The prompt artifact list is the fallback specification. Official JSON-schema conformance cannot be established; syntactically valid JSON and local integrity checks are not schema validation.

The unmodified shipped script is not executable end to end in the headless environment; it stops at View(), and a headless-only adaptation stops at the omitted GMHWG object. Numerical reproduction after transparent repairs must not be read as execution success of the unmodified archive.

Three numerical claim groups only partly match under primary R 4.6.1. A targeted same-data, same-call check under R 4.2.2 recovers both discrepant confidence intervals; the W=1037.5 versus 1137.5 discrepancy persists. The original exact runtime was not shipped, so R 4.2.2 is not asserted to be the authors’ actual version.

No signed nanopublications or public report repository were published. nanopubs/PUBLISHED.md explicitly records that no result URIs exist; a field-by-field draft chain is supplied. Human identity, ORCID, signing credentials, and public repository URL were not supplied or transmitted.

This certifies numerical computational agreement only. Scientific validity, the suitability of statistical tests, robustness under alternative methods, and independent replication with new data were not assessed.

The locked Pixi environment was created locally and all 148 R packages were restored into an empty library, followed by a full workflow rerun. A rebuild on a second host has not been tested; macOS framework R 4.6.1 and Apple build tools remain host prerequisites.

pilot_constraints.note: Host R, Python, compilers, and PDF utility were invoked; no existing local study, report, skill file, or instruction file outside the pilot directory was opened.
